title: Keyboard navigation, skip-link, and landmark roles
iWant: to reach and operate every part of the application without a pointer
soThat: the application is fully usable with the keyboard alone

acceptanceCriteria.description: A skip-link is the first focusable element on every route, visible on focus, and moves focus to the main content region.
acceptanceCriteria.when: Tab is pressed once from page load
acceptanceCriteria.then: the skip-link receives visible focus and activating it moves focus into main

acceptanceCriteria.description: Tab and Shift-Tab traverse all interactive elements in a logical order matching the visual order.
acceptanceCriteria.when: the page is traversed with Tab and Shift-Tab
acceptanceCriteria.then: focus order matches visual order with no unreachable interactive element

acceptanceCriteria.description: Arrow keys move between items inside menus and menu-like composites; Tab exits the composite rather than walking every item.
acceptanceCriteria.when: arrow keys and Tab are pressed
acceptanceCriteria.then: arrows move within the menu and Tab moves focus out of it

acceptanceCriteria.description: Escape closes the topmost open overlay (menu, modal, drawer, popover) and returns focus to the element that opened it.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the overlay closes and focus returns to its trigger

acceptanceCriteria.description: Shell regions expose landmark roles: banner, navigation, main, and contentinfo; exactly one main per route.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the four landmarks are present and main is unique

acceptanceCriteria.description: No keyboard trap exists anywhere: from any focused element, the user can always move focus away using standard keys.
acceptanceCriteria.given: any interactive element on any route
acceptanceCriteria.then: focus always has an exit path
